# CLAUDE.md - bit-monitoring

## Project Overview
BIT Monitoring - Internal monitoring and alerting system for Bureau-IT to monitor all client cloud resources from a single dashboard.

## Workspace Sync
Ao finalizar sessão significativa (PRs merged, features, mudança de fase), atualizar `~/Projetos/GitHub/claude-workspace/projects/bit-monitoring.md`.

## Tech Stack
- **Backend**: Python 3.11+ / FastAPI 0.125 / Celery 5.3 / python-socketio 5.14
- **Frontend**: Next.js 16 / React 19 / React Query 5 / NextAuth 4 / Tailwind CSS 3.4
- **Database**: PostgreSQL 15+ / TimescaleDB
- **Cache/Queue**: Redis 7+
- **Deployment**: Docker Compose (dev) / GitHub Actions CI/CD → AWS ECR → EC2 via SSM (prod)

## Project Structure
```
bit-monitoring/
├── docker-compose.yml      # Container orchestration
├── .env.example            # Environment template
├── backend/                # Python FastAPI + Celery
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── api/v1/         # REST endpoints
│   │   ├── core/           # Security, encryption, sync/async DB
│   │   ├── models/         # SQLAlchemy models
│   │   ├── schemas/        # Pydantic validation schemas
│   │   ├── services/       # Business logic (alerts, MFA, magic link, realtime)
│   │   ├── providers/      # Cloud provider abstractions
│   │   │   ├── base.py     # Interfaces (multi-cloud)
│   │   │   └── aws/        # AWS implementation
│   │   ├── monitors/       # Uptime, Docker checks
│   │   └── notifications/  # Alert channels
│   ├── workers/            # Celery tasks
│   ├── scripts/            # Helper scripts (VAPID keys, broadcast notifications, etc.)
│   ├── alembic/            # Database migrations
│   └── tests/              # Test suite
├── frontend/               # Next.js dashboard
│   ├── src/app/            # App router pages
│   └── public/sw.js        # Service worker (browser push)
├── nginx/                  # Reverse proxy config
└── docs/                   # Documentation
```

## Development Commands
```bash
# Start all services
docker-compose up -d

# View logs
docker-compose logs -f backend

# Run backend tests
docker-compose exec backend pytest

# Database migrations
docker-compose exec backend alembic upgrade head

# Restart specific service
docker-compose restart backend
```

## Git Workflow

**IMPORTANT: Direct pushes to `master` are not allowed.** All changes must go through a Pull Request.

The repository has CI enforcement that will automatically revert any direct pushes to master.

### How to make changes:
```bash
# 1. Create a feature branch
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name

# 2. Make your changes and commit
git add .
git commit -m "Description of changes"

# 3. Push to remote
git push -u origin feature/your-feature-name

# 4. Create a Pull Request
gh pr create --title "Your PR title" --body "Description"

# 5. After review/approval, merge the PR
gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
```

### Documentation Updates with PRs
**IMPORTANT:** When creating a PR, always check and update documentation to keep it in sync:
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — Update Current Status, Key Features, or other sections affected by the change
- **`docs/backlog.md`** — Mark completed items, add new items if applicable
- **`memory/MEMORY.md`** — Update completed phases, lessons learned, or architecture notes

Documentation should go upstream already up-to-date with the code changes, not as a separate follow-up.

### Branch naming conventions:
- `feature/` - New features
- `fix/` - Bug fixes
- `docs/` - Documentation updates
- `refactor/` - Code refactoring
```

## CI/CD Pipeline
- **Trigger**: Push to `master` branch (via merged PR only)
- **Workflow**: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
- **Stages**: PR enforcement → Security scan → Tests → Build & push to ECR → Deploy to EC2 via SSM → Broadcast deploy notification (if PR has `## What's New`)
- **ECR Registry**: `521754968346.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/bit-monitoring/{backend,frontend}`
- **Deploy mechanism**: AWS SSM RunCommand → `scripts/deploy.sh` (git pull → ECR pull → docker compose up → nginx reload)
- **Production URL**: https://status.bureau-it.com
- **SSH alias**: `ssh bit-monitoring` (EC2 instance `i-0f909f8f77776fcf0`, IP `54.237.114.115`)

### Deploy Notifications Convention
The CI/CD pipeline extracts the `## What's New` section from the PR body after deploy and broadcasts it as an in-app notification to all users.

**IMPORTANT:** When creating a PR, always ask the user: *"Should this deploy notify users? If so, what should the message say?"* Then include a `## What's New` section in the PR body only if the user confirms. Keep the message short (1-2 sentences), user-friendly (no technical jargon), and actionable.

### Required GitHub Secrets
`AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `EC2_INSTANCE_ID`, `DOMAIN`

### Required IAM
- **EC2 role** (`bit-monitoring-ec2-role`): `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`, `AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryPowerUser`
- **CI/CD user** (`bit-monitoring-cicd`): ECR push + `ssm:SendCommand` + `ssm:GetCommandInvocation`

| nginx | 80, 443 | Reverse proxy, SSL |
| frontend | 3000 | Next.js dashboard |

## Key Features
- AWS resource monitoring (EC2, RDS, Route53, CloudFront, ALB, ACM)
- EC2 instance management (start/stop/reboot) for superadmins
- Website uptime monitoring with HTTP retries (3 attempts), recovery threshold (anti-flapping), SSL expiry alerts, and dedicated Celery worker
- Cost tracking via AWS Cost Explorer with budgets and forecasting
- Incident management with acknowledge/resolve workflow and bulk actions
- Multi-channel alerting (Email, Slack, ClickUp, Twilio SMS/WhatsApp, Webhook)
- Real-time push notifications (WebSocket via Socket.IO + browser push via VAPID)
- In-app notification center with read/unread tracking
- Notification preferences per user (severity filters, trigger filters, quiet hours)
- Client status pages with token-based public access per client
- Public status page for transparent uptime communication
- System update notifications (automated via CI/CD with `## What's New` PR convention)
- Audit logging with security event tracking
- Role-based access control (superadmin/admin/viewer)
- User invitation system (email-based onboarding with secure token links)
- Multi-Factor Authentication (TOTP) with backup codes
- Magic Link passwordless login (email-based)
- User account management (profile, password, security, notification preferences)
- Dark/Light theme toggle
- Zoom user sync via S2S OAuth (Educational account)
- Stripe multi-account integration (Brazil + US regions)
- Unified Clients page with Zoom+Stripe matching
- Infrastructure monitoring via OpenTelemetry Collector (host CPU/memory/disk/network + Docker container stats)
- CloudWatch metrics polling for managed AWS services (RDS, ALB, CloudFront) with per-resource charts
- CloudWatch alert thresholds (8 critical rules: RDS CPU/Memory/Storage/DiskQueue, ALB Unhealthy/5XX/Rejected, CF 5XX)
- BIT Agent Diagnostics: auto-dispatch read-only diagnostic commands to agents for incident triage
- Onboarding guided tour (driver.js) for new and existing users on first login
- Dashboard overview with infra agents health, recent incidents, down monitors, role-based quick actions

- **Monitor Scheduling Fix**: COMPLETE (PR #92) — fixed last_check drift causing 2-3 gaps/hour in uptime bars
- **Recovery Threshold (Anti-Flapping)**: COMPLETE (PR #96) — require N consecutive successes before auto-resolving incidents (hysteresis pattern)
- **Next**: Phase 7c-7d (ECS/EKS, multi-cloud) — see docs/backlog.md for full backlog

## Infrastructure Monitoring (Phase 7a)
- **Architecture**: OTel Collector agents on target servers push metrics via OTLP/HTTP protobuf → Backend API → TimescaleDB hypertable → Celery alert evaluation
- **OTLP Receiver**: `POST /api/v1/otel/v1/metrics` (protobuf, per-agent bearer token auth — not JWT)
- **Agent CRUD**: `/api/v1/otel-agents/` (admin-only, token shown once at creation, SHA-256 hashed)
- **Metrics Query**: `/api/v1/infra-metrics/summary` and `/agents/{id}/metrics`
- **Models**: `OtelAgent` (agent registry + `consecutive_heartbeat_failures` + `heartbeat_failure_threshold`), `InfraMetric` (TimescaleDB hypertable, 30-day retention)
- **Celery Tasks**: `evaluate_infra_alerts` (every 2min), `check_agent_heartbeats` (every 5min)
- **Alert TriggerTypes**: `HOST_METRIC_THRESHOLD`, `CONTAINER_METRIC_THRESHOLD`, `CLOUDWATCH_METRIC_THRESHOLD`
- **Heartbeat Consecutive Failures**: OTel agents threshold=2 (~10 min), CloudWatch agents threshold=3 (~15 min). Silent recovery if below threshold.

## CloudWatch Metrics Polling (Phase 7b)
- **Architecture**: Celery task polls CloudWatch every 5 min per account → stores in same InfraMetric hypertable via virtual `OtelAgent` entries (agent_type="cloudwatch")
- **Poller**: `backend/app/providers/aws/cloudwatch.py` — metric definitions, virtual agent lifecycle, batched GetMetricData API
- **Celery Task**: `workers/tasks/cloudwatch.py` → `poll_cloudwatch_metrics` (every 5 min)
- **Metrics**: 23 total — 10 RDS, 9 ALB (6 standard + 3 target-group-scoped), 4 CloudFront
- **ALB Target Groups**: Discovered via `elbv2.describe_target_groups`, metrics use dual dimensions (LoadBalancer + TargetGroup)
- **CloudFront**: All queries go to `us-east-1` with `Region=Global` dimension
- **Alert Evaluation**: `CLOUDWATCH_METRIC_THRESHOLD` trigger type, 10-min lookback minimum, auto-resolve when below threshold
- **Alert Thresholds**: 25 rules created via `backend/scripts/create_cloudwatch_alert_rules.py` (8 critical enabled, 17 warnings disabled)
- **Active Critical Rules**: RDS CPU>90%, Memory<64MB, Storage<2GB, DiskQueue>64; ALB UnhealthyHosts>0, ELB5XX>25, RejectedConn>0; CF 5XX>5%
- **Frontend**: Detail page groups charts by resource type (RDS/ALB/CF), AreaChart with multi-resource support, per-section color palettes
- **Toggle**: Per-account `cloudwatch_enabled` setting in Cloud Accounts admin
- **Metrics Audit**: `docs/cloudwatch-metrics-audit.md`

## 🎯 Proposta de integração `bit-waf` ↔ `bit-monitoring`

### O que descobri sobre bit-monitoring

- **Stack:** FastAPI + Celery + PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB + Next.js
- **Modelo `AlertRule`:** db record com `metric` (string), `operator`, `threshold`, `duration`, `severity`, `notification_channel_ids`, `cooldown`
- **Modelo `NotificationRule`:** define como roteia, com `trigger_type` enum (já tem `CLOUDWATCH_METRIC_THRESHOLD`)
- **Poller:** `cloudwatch.py` em `backend/app/providers/aws/` — define métricas a coletar a cada 5min, normaliza nomes (ex: `aws.cloudfront.5xx_error_rate`), guarda em TimescaleDB
- **Métricas suportadas hoje:** RDS (10), ALB (9), CloudFront (4)
- **Sem suporte AWS WAF nativamente** ainda (não vi `aws.wafv2.*` no poller)

### 3 níveis de integração possíveis

#### Nível 1 — Tagging (mais simples)

Quando `apply-rule.sh` cria/modifica rule WAF, criar **alarm CloudWatch nativo** (não bit-monitoring) com tags:
```
AWSManagedBy=bit-waf
Site=concertacao
RuleName=RateLimit-300-Block
```

bit-monitoring pode (eventualmente) descobrir esses alarms via tag e importá-los.

**Pró:** zero acoplamento, não precisa mexer no bit-monitoring.
**Contra:** alarms não aparecem no dashboard do bit-monitoring até alguém adicionar suporte lá.

#### Nível 2 — Templates declaram alarms + apply-rule cria via API bit-monitoring (recomendado)

Cada template em `templates/rules/*.json` ganha um campo `_meta.alarms`:

```json
{
  "_meta": {
    "name": "rate-limit-generic",
    "alarms": [
      {
        "name": "WAF RateLimit Spike",
        "description": "Rate limit blocks > 50/5min — pode indicar threshold mal calibrado OU ataque",
        "resource_type": "wafv2",
        "metric": "aws.wafv2.blocked_requests",
        "metric_dimensions": {
          "WebACL": "{{WEB_ACL_NAME}}",
          "Rule": "{{RULE_NAME}}"
        },
        "operator": ">",
        "threshold": "50",
        "duration": 300,
        "severity": "warning"
      }
    ]
  },
  "rule": { ... }
}
```

`apply-rule.sh` ao final:
1. Aplica rule no WAF (já faz)
2. Para cada alarm declarado, faz `POST /api/v1/alert-rules` no bit-monitoring com substituição dos placeholders
3. bit-monitoring começa a evaluar a métrica e enviar notificação se threshold for cruzado

**Pré-requisitos no bit-monitoring:**
- Adicionar suporte WAF no poller (`backend/app/providers/aws/cloudwatch.py`) — namespace `AWS/WAFV2`, métricas `BlockedRequests`, `AllowedRequests`, `CountedRequests`, dimensões `WebACL` + `Rule` + `Region`
- API key/token p/ apply-rule.sh autenticar
- Idempotência: se alarm já existe, update ao invés de criar duplicado

**Pró:** zero tocar diretamente no CloudWatch, alarms já entram no dashboard, notification routing reaproveitado.
**Contra:** depende de adicionar suporte WAF no bit-monitoring (1 PR no poller + migrations).

#### Nível 3 — Bidirecional

Bit-monitoring detecta padrão recorrente (alarm WAF dispara 5x na mesma rule em 30 dias) e abre **issue** ou notificação proativa: "rule X tem threshold mal calibrado, considerar revisar via `/audit-acl`".

**Pró:** feedback loop fechado.
**Contra:** complexidade alta, baixo ROI inicial. Adiar para depois de Nível 2 estar provado.

### Minha recomendação: Nível 2 em 2 fases

#### Fase A (no bit-monitoring): adicionar suporte WAF

1. **PR no bit-monitoring** com:
   - Adicionar `wafv2` em `cloudwatch.py` poller (namespace `AWS/WAFV2`, métricas `BlockedRequests`/`AllowedRequests`/`CountedRequests`, dimensões `WebACL`/`Rule`/`Region`)
   - Atualizar `cloudwatch-metrics-audit.md` com seção WAF
   - Criar alert rules WAF base no `create_cloudwatch_alert_rules.py` (ex: "WAF total blocks > 500/5min" como sentinel global)
   - Token de API para clients externos (apply-rule precisa autenticar)
   - Endpoint idempotente `PUT /api/v1/alert-rules/upsert` (cria ou atualiza por nome)

2. **Provavelmente reaproveitar:** discovery de WebACL via cloud_account model (similar ao que já faz pra CF). Cada conta AWS habilitada já lista distribuições — adicionar WebACLs.

#### Fase B (no bit-waf): consumir API

1. **Adicionar campo `_meta.alarms`** em cada template `templates/rules/*.json` com spec do alarm correspondente
2. **Helper `apply-rule.sh`** ganha step 9 opcional: se template declara alarms e env var `BIT_MONITORING_API_TOKEN` está setada, faz upsert via API
3. **`waf-sites.yaml`** ganha campo `bit_monitoring_url` + `bit_monitoring_token` por site
4. **Argumento `--no-alarms`** para skip (caso queira aplicar rule sem criar alarm)

### Custo estimado

- **Fase A (bit-monitoring):** 1 dia (adicionar poller WAF + migration + alert rules base + endpoint upsert)
- **Fase B (bit-waf):** 2-3h (estender templates + apply-rule step 9 + docs)
- **Total:** ~1.5 dia de trabalho + tempo de PR review/deploy do bit-monitoring

### Alternativa rápida (Nível 1) se quiser entregar hoje

Se preferir entregar **algo agora sem mexer no bit-monitoring**, posso fazer Nível 1 em ~30min: `apply-rule.sh` cria alarm CloudWatch nativo com naming convention `bit-waf-{site}-{rule}-{type}` e tag `AWSManagedBy=bit-waf`. Quando bit-monitoring ganhar suporte WAF (Fase A futura), descobre esses alarms automaticamente via tag.

## Análise Estruturada: Backend Models + Services da PR #139 (Attack Monitoring)

### 1. **Modelo de Dados — SecurityEvent (Hypertable)**

A tabela `security_events` armazena **um evento por linha** (1 row = 1 request bloqueado), não agregado. Campos críticos:
- **Identificação**: `id` (BigInteger), `timestamp` (timezone-aware, indexed)
- **Fonte**: `source` ("waf_cloudfront" | "waf_alb") — **sem CloudFront explícito separado**
- **Regra**: `rule_name` (quer aqui o `terminatingRuleId` do WAF)
- **Geo/Org**: `country_code`, `ip_org`, `ip_city`, `ip_asn` (enriquecimento async)
- **Request**: `uri`, `http_method`, `user_agent`, `status_code`
- **Threat**: `bot_category` (WAF BotCategory), `threat_score` (população futura)

**Detalhe crítico**: Não há campo `web_acl_id` ou `web_acl_name` — apenas `rule_name`. Isso limita drill-down por Web ACL específica. Constraint único: `(source, timestamp, ip_address, rule_name)` para deduplicação via `on_conflict_do_nothing`.

### 2. **Storage & Compression (Alembic)**

- **Hypertable**: chunks de 1 dia (TimescaleDB)
- **Compression**: ativada após 7 dias (~60% savings)
- **Retention**: 90 dias (compliance)
- **Continuous Aggregate**: `attack_timeline_1h` (5 min refresh) agrupa por `(hour, source, action, count)`

Fallback inteligente: se contínuo falhar, cria VIEW SQL regular (mais lento, sem refresh automático).

### 3. **Coleta de Logs — WafCollectorService**

Consome **CloudWatch Logs Insights** (não S3) para ambas as fontes:
- Log groups: `aws-waf-logs-concertacao` (CloudFront) e `aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb` (ALB)
- Query: filtra `action = 'BLOCK'`, extrai `terminatingRuleId`, `clientIp`, `country`, `uri`, `httpMethod`, User-Agent
- Polling assíncrono: start_query → poll até "Complete" (timeout 60s)
- **Worker**: Celery task `collect_waf_events` roda **a cada 5 min**, usa watermark por source (last_ts + 1s)

**Sem CloudFront adicional**: código trata "waf_cloudfront" como genérico — não diferencia CF vs distribution IDs.

### 4. **Enriquecimento IP (IpEnrichmentService)**

- **Fonte**: ip-api.com (free tier: 45 req/min)
- **Cache**: Redis, TTL 7 dias
- **Rate-limit**: batches de 9 IPs, sleep 12s entre batches
- **Fallback**: retorna `{}` se API falhar — evento é ingerido mesmo sem geo

### 5. **Camada de Serviço (SecurityService)**

Métodos públicos reutilizáveis:
- `get_attack_summary(hours)` — top rules, IPs, ASNs, countries, timeline
- `get_top_attackers(hours, limit)` — ranked por IP com geo
- `list_events(hours, source, rule, page, page_size)` — filtrado e paginado
- `_top_n(field, since)` — genérico para qualquer coluna
- `_timeline(since)` — tenta aggregate contínuo, fallback SQL

**Superfícies de extensão**: métodos não expõem `count_blocks_by_rule_id(rule, window)` — isso seria necessário para bit-waf injetar alertas operacionais por rule específica.

### 6. **Notificação — TriggerType + Spike Detection**

- Enum `TriggerType` agora inclui `SECURITY_ATTACK`
- Task `detect_attack_spike` (15 min): Z-score (3σ) vs. baseline 7 dias, dispara alerta se `current > threshold && current > 10`
- Alerta carrega top rule e top IP nos details

### **Perguntas Respondidas:**

✅ **Evento vs. agregado**: Evento (1:1)  
✅ **WAF Logs**: CloudWatch Logs Insights, não S3  
✅ **CloudFront**: Genérico "waf_cloudfront", sem multi-distribution  
✅ **Extensibilidade**: `SecurityService._top_n()` reutilizável, mas faltam métodos granulares por rule

## Análise da PR #139 — bit-monitoring: WAF Collector + Auth

### 1. **Coleta de Eventos & Scheduling**

`collect_waf_events` (executado a cada **5 min**) é **monolítica com 2 iterações hardcoded**:

```python
for source, fetch_fn in [
    ("waf_cloudfront", collector.query_cloudfront_waf),
    ("waf_alb", collector.query_alb_waf),
]:
```

Os **log groups estão hardcoded** em `waf_collector.py`:
- CloudFront: `aws-waf-logs-concertacao` (fixo)
- ALB: `aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb` (fixo)

**Watermark por fonte**: armazena `max(SecurityEvent.timestamp)` por `source` no DB. Avança +1s para evitar reprocessar evento de fronteira. Query CloudWatch Logs Insights filtra por `action = 'BLOCK'` e extrai: `@timestamp, terminatingRuleId, httpRequest.{clientIp, uri, country, httpMethod}`. Upsert via `on_conflict_do_nothing` com constraint único `(source, timestamp, ip_address, rule_name)` — dedup automático.

**Problema extensibilidade**: adicionar novo WAF (ex: CloudFront em outra conta) exigiria hardcoding + redeploy. Não há config table.

---

### 2. **Spike Detection — Caminho Próprio**

`detect_attack_spike` (15 min) **não usa AlertRule existente**. Implementa **3σ (3 standard deviations)**:
- Baseline: média dos últimos 7 dias em buckets de 15 min
- Threshold: `mean + 3 * stddev`
- Trigger: `current_count > threshold AND current_count > 10`

Dispara via `SyncAlertService.trigger_alert(TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK)` — **tipo dedicado**, não reutiliza regras do alerting general.

---

### 3. **Endpoints Security — GET-only**

`backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/security.py` (4 endpoints, todos `GET`):
- `/summary` — agregado últimas 24h (param: `hours`)
- `/events` — lista com filtros (`source`, `rule`, paginação 1-500 items)
- `/timeline` — agregação por hora/fonte (suporta continuous aggregate TimescaleDB)
- `/top-attackers` — IPs enriquecidos com geo/org (limite 100)

**Nenhum POST/PUT** → `apply-rule.sh` **não pode criar alertas diretamente**. Precisa chamar `/api/v1/alert-rules` (em `alert_rules.py`).

---

### 4. **AlertRules CRUD Existe — Admin-only**

`alert_rules.py` oferece **POST** para criar regras:
```python
@router.post("", response_model=AlertRuleResponse, status_code=201)
async def create_alert_rule(
    data: AlertRuleCreate,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_admin),  # ← admin obrigatório
):
```

Campos: `name, description, resource_type, resource_id, metric, operator, threshold, duration, severity, cooldown`. **Ponto de extensão viável para apply-rule.sh** — mas requer credenciais admin.

---

### 5. **Autenticação: bit-auth SSO + JWT local**

`auth.py` (linha 564-626) implementa **OAuth2 code flow** contra `BIT_AUTH_URL`:
1. Redireciona para `/oauth/authorize`
2. Callback recebe `code` → troca por `access_token` (via `/oauth/token`)
3. Decodifica JWT localmente: `decode_bit_auth_token(token, BIT_AUTH_SECRET_KEY)`
4. Sincroniza usuário em DB (ou cria com senha aleatória não-usada)
5. Emite **JWT local** para manter compatibilidade interna

**`bit_auth_client.py` (35 linhas)**:
- `decode_bit_auth_token()` — valida JWT HS256 localmente (compartilha secret)
- `get_userinfo()` — fallback HTTP para `/userinfo` do bit-auth

**Config (config.py)**:
```python
BIT_AUTH_URL: str = "http://localhost:8200"
BIT_AUTH_SECRET_KEY: str = ""  # ← deve ser igual ao bit-auth
BIT_AUTH_CLIENT_ID: str = "bit-monitoring"
BIT_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET: str = "bit-monitoring-secret-change-in-prod"
```

**Chamada remota (ex: apply-rule.sh em outra máquina)**:
1. Obter token via `/api/v1/auth/sso/login` → redireciona para bit-auth
2. Ou compartilhar `BIT_AUTH_SECRET_KEY` + emitir JWT local direto
3. Usar `Authorization: Bearer <token>` nas chamadas REST

---

### 6. **Pub/Sub para SecurityEvents**

`RealtimeService` (in `app/services/realtime.py`) publica via **Redis pub/sub**:
```python
RealtimeService.publish_event_sync(
    event_type="security_event",
    data={"timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()},
)
```

Subscribers via WebSocket (`ws.py`): permite dashboard real-time, **mas não há consumer externo dedicado** para alert engine. Pub/sub é broadcast — qualquer aplicação pode escutar `EVENTS_CHANNEL` Redis, mas não há integração pré-configurada.

---

### 7. **CloudFront WAF — Já Incluído (ALB Não Exclusive)**

PR **já coleta CloudFront WAF**:
- Log group: `aws-waf-logs-concertacao`
- Query Insights: mesmo SQL para ambos os WAFs
- `source="waf_cloudfront"` vs `source="waf_alb"` — discriminado no DB

**Extensão para múltiplas distribuições**: seria parametrizar `CLOUDFRONT_LOG_GROUP` ou ler de config table ao invés de hardcode. Não há fork necessário — estrutura já permite.

---

## Resumo: Pontos de Extensão para apply-rule.sh

1. **Criar alertas programaticamente**: `POST /api/v1/alert-rules` (requer admin JWT) — **viável**
2. **Autenticação remota**: usar bit-auth SSO ou compartilhar `BIT_AUTH_SECRET_KEY` para emitir JWT local
3. **Escalabilidade WAF**: refatorar log groups em config table/env, iterar parametricamente
4. **Monitoramento spike**: integrar com AlertRule existente ao invés de caminho próprio (TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK poderia verificar rules antes de disparo)
5. **Consumidor alertas**: RealtimeService já pub/sub-ready — alerting engine pode escutar Redis `EVENTS_CHANNEL` em paralelo

## Relatório: Arquitetura de Alertas no bit-monitoring (master)

### 1. **Endpoints de AlertRule — Existe, Autenticação Admin**

A API oferece endpoints **POST/PUT/DELETE** em `/api/v1/alert-rules`:

- **POST `/alert-rules`** → `create_alert_rule(AlertRuleCreate)` — requer `get_current_admin`
- **PUT `/alert-rules/{rule_id}`** → `update_alert_rule(...)` — requer admin
- **DELETE `/alert-rules/{rule_id}`** — admin-only
- **GET `/alert-rules`** — listar (user comum pode ler)

Status HTTP: **201 Created** para POST, **204 No Content** para DELETE. Auditoria automática (AuditLog) em todas operações.

**Crítico para bit-waf**: `apply-rule.sh` pode fazer POST via Bearer token de admin (API key) para criar AlertRule programaticamente.

---

### 2. **AlertRule NÃO Suporta Dimensions — Limitação Atual**

O modelo `AlertRule` **não possui campo `dimensions`** ou `metadata`. Estrutura fixa:

```python
AlertRule:
  name, description
  resource_type: str (enum: host, docker, rds, alb, cloudfront)
  resource_id: Optional[int]  # ← Específico, não arb. dimensions
  metric: str (max 100 chars)
  operator: str (>, <, ==, !=, >=, <=)
  threshold: str
  duration: int (segundos)
  severity: AlertSeverity (info/warning/critical)
  notification_channel_ids: JSON[] (IDs de canais)
  cooldown: int (segundos)
  is_active: bool
```

**Problema**: Para WAF, queremos diferençar alarmes por:
- `WebACL=ACL-WPAdminHML` vs `WebACL=ACL-AdminDash`
- `Rule=RateLimit-300-Block` vs `Rule=IPReputation-Block`
- `Region=us-east-1` vs `Region=sa-east-1`

Mas só há `resource_id` (int) e `resource_type` (string pré-validado). **Solução**: Adicionar coluna `JSON` type ao model e schema.

---

### 3. **Como CloudWatch Poller Usa Dimensions Hoje**

O `cloudwatch.py` constrói queries CloudWatch explicitamente com `Dimensions`:

```python
dimensions = [
    {"Name": config["dimension_key"], "Value": dimension_value},
]
# Ex: {"Name": "DBInstanceIdentifier", "Value": "prod-db"}
# Ex: {"Name": "LoadBalancer", "Value": "app/my-alb/xyz"}
# Ex: {"Name": "DistributionId", "Value": "E123ABC"}
```

CloudFront extra: `{"Name": "Region", "Value": "Global"}`

As métricas são **hardcoded por resource type** (RDS, ALB, CloudFront). **WAF seria novo**: não existe suporte CloudWatch para métrica `BlockedRequests` por WAF Rule específica (só agregados).

---

### 4. **NotificationRule + TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK Já Existe**

O enum `TriggerType` já inclui:

```python
SECURITY_ATTACK = "security_attack"
```

Pronto para usar. A WAF CollectorService já escreve em `SecurityEvent` e pode disparar alertas via `TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK`. **Fluxo**:
1. WAF logs coletados → `SecurityEvent` table
2. Detecção de spike → `SyncAlertService.trigger_alert(TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK, ...)`
3. `trigger_alert` acha `NotificationRule` com `trigger_type=SECURITY_ATTACK`
4. Cria `Incident` + enfileira notificações (Slack, email, etc.)

---

### 5. **Frontend `/security` — Sistema Completo (PR #139)**

Página nova com:
- **Summarys**: total/24h, top IP, países, rules
- **Timeline Chart**: recharts (TBD bucket size)
- **Rules Breakdown**: por rule_name
- **Recent Events Table**: últimos eventos
- **WebSocket**: real-time updates via `useWebSocket`

Queries chamam `/api/v1/security/summary`, `/events`, `/timeline`, `/top-attackers`. **Não vê alertas/regras de WAF via AlertRule** — apenas eventos e agregações.

---

### 6. **Região Hardcoded vs. Config**

CloudWatch polling: região extraída de `Resource.region`. AlertRule não tem campo `region`. **Observação**: `sa-east-1` usado em variáveis globais, mas código é agnóstico.

---

### 7. **25 Rules Existentes — RDS/ALB/CloudFront Apenas**

`create_cloudwatch_alert_rules.py` cria 25 regras:
- **12 RDS** (CPU, memória, latência, I/O)
- **8 ALB** (erros, conexões, tempo resposta)
- **4 CloudFront** (4XX/5XX rates)
- **1 EC2 Host** (CPU)

Nenhuma WAF. Format simples: `metric > threshold` para duração X segundos.

---

## **Resumo — Resposta às Perguntas Críticas**

| Pergunta | Resposta |
|----------|----------|
| **POST/PUT AlertRule via API?** | ✅ SIM — `/alert-rules`, requer admin auth. Auditado. |
| **Suporta dimensions arbitrárias?** | ❌ NÃO hoje. Só `resource_type` (pré-validado) + `resource_id` (int). Precisa migração: adicionar `JSON metadata` ao modelo. |
| **CloudWatch poller + WAF?** | ❌ NÃO — CloudWatch não expõe bloqueios por rule WAF. Métrica seria custom (precisaria Lambda/EventBridge ou parse WAF logs direto). |
| **Frontend aba "WAF Rules"?** | Pode ser `/security/rules-breakdown` que já existe em PR #139. Ou estender AlertRule para suportar WAF rules com dimensions. |
| **Provider/region separado?** | Não. AlertRule assume um resource_type genérico. Região vem do Resource ou está em CloudWatch dimensions implícitas. |

---

## **Ação para bit-waf/apply-rule.sh**

1. **Migração de schema** (1h): Adicionar `metadata: JSON` a `AlertRule` + schemas Pydantic
2. **Exemplo POST**: 
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://api/alert-rules \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_API_KEY}" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "name": "WAF RateLimit-300-Block Blocked Requests High",
       "resource_type": "waf",
       "metric": "BlockedRequests",
       "operator": ">",
       "threshold": "100",

       },
       "severity": "warning"
     }'
   ```
3. **Webhook/Poller** (2h): Sistema externo (não CloudWatch) que coleta métricas WAF por rule + dimensions e dispara `trigger_alert(TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK, ...)`

**Rota recomendada**: Usar `NotificationRule(TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK)` existente + estender WAF collector com suporte a dimension-aware alerting via AlertRule customizável.

## O que PR #139 entregou

**Camada de eventos (granular):**
- `SecurityEvent` (TimescaleDB hypertable, 1 linha/request bloqueado, retenção 90d, compressão 7d)
- `WafCollectorService` via CloudWatch Logs Insights — log groups **hardcoded** (`aws-waf-logs-concertacao` CF + `aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb`)
- `SecurityService.get_attack_summary/list_events/top_attackers/timeline`
- `detect_attack_spike` via 3σ → dispara `TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK` (caminho **próprio**, não usa AlertRule)
- Frontend `/security` com KPIs, timeline, rules breakdown, top attackers
- SSO bit-auth + JWT local

**Sistema de AlertRule pré-existente (master):**
- `POST /api/v1/alert-rules` (admin-only, auditado)
- Modelo: `resource_type` (host/docker/rds/alb/cloudfront) + `resource_id` + `metric` + `operator` + `threshold`
- **NÃO tem campo `dimensions`/`metadata` JSON** — limitação chave
- CloudWatch poller hoje cobre RDS/ALB/CF, **não WAF**

## Gaps que bit-waf precisa preencher

| # | Gap | Impacto |
|---|-----|---------|
| 1 | `SecurityEvent` não tem `web_acl_id`/`web_acl_name` — só `rule_name` | Não dá pra distinguir mesma rule em ACLs diferentes (multi-site) |
| 2 | Log groups WAF hardcoded em código | Adicionar novo site exige redeploy |
| 3 | `AlertRule` sem `dimensions`/`metadata` JSON | `apply-rule.sh` não consegue criar alarme "BlockedRequests da rule X na ACL Y" |
| 4 | `resource_type` enum não tem `waf` | Bloqueia AlertRule pra WAF |
| 5 | `detect_attack_spike` ignora AlertRule existente | Threshold 3σ é fixo, não configurável por usuário |
| 6 | Sem método `count_blocks_by_rule(rule_name, web_acl, window)` em SecurityService | Frontend e alert engine não conseguem drill-down por rule |

## Proposta de extensão (em cima da PR #139, não substituindo)

**Branch:** `feat/waf-alert-rules-extension` (parte da `feat/security-attack-monitoring`, vai pra mesma PR ou stack em cima)

### Fatia 1 — Schema (migração leve)
- `SecurityEvent`: adicionar `web_acl_id`, `web_acl_name`, `region` (NOT NULL com default na migração)
- `AlertRule`: adicionar `dimensions JSONB` + estender enum `resource_type` com `waf`
- Atualizar `WafCollectorService.query_*` pra extrair `webaclId` do log

- `collect_waf_events` itera sobre config em vez de loop hardcoded de 2

- `POST /api/v1/alert-rules/upsert` (idempotente por `name`) com `dimensions`
- Token machine-to-machine (service account no bit-auth ou shared secret)
- `apply-rule.sh` chama ao instalar uma rule, criando alarme baseline `BlockedRequests > N/5min`

- `detect_attack_spike` consulta AlertRules com `resource_type='waf'` e usa threshold custom em vez de 3σ fixo (mantém 3σ como fallback)

Para cada AlertRule:\n   - Ler `dimensions` (campo JSON da Fatia 1) — espera-se `{\"web_acl_id\":..., \"rule_name\":..., \"metric\":\"BlockedRequests\"}` ou similar\n   - Calcular contagem na janela `duration` segundos pra `(rule_name, web_acl_id)` da AlertRule (usando `SecurityService.count_blocks_by_rule` da Fatia 4 — se ainda não existir, fazer query SQL inline com TODO de refactor)\n   - Comparar com `threshold` da AlertRule\n   - Se `count operator threshold` (operator = `>`/`>=`/etc.) → disparar `trigger_alert(TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK, ...)` com `alert_rule_id` no payload\n3. **Fallback 3σ existente**: pra `(rule_name, web_acl_id)` que NÃO tem AlertRule explícita, manter detecção 3σ atual como segurança (zero-config protection)\n4. **Cooldown**: respeitar `cooldown` da AlertRule (campo já existe no model). Hoje detect_attack_spike tem cooldown próprio — usar o da AlertRule quando ela existe, fallback hardcoded quando não.\n\n### Implementação\n\nRefatorar `detect_attack_spike` task em `backend/workers/tasks/waf_collector.py`:\n\n```python\n@celery_app.task\ndef detect_attack_spike():\n    db = get_sync_db_session()\n    try:\n        # 1. Custom AlertRules\n        custom_rules = db.execute(\n            select(AlertRule).where(\n                AlertRule.resource_type == \"waf\",\n                AlertRule.is_active == True,\n            )\n        ).scalars().all()\n        \n        triggered_pairs = set()  # (rule_name, web_acl_id) já tratados\n        \n        for ar in custom_rules:\n            dims = ar.dimensions or {}\n            rule_name = dims.get(\"rule_name\")\n            web_acl_id = dims.get(\"web_acl_id\")\n            if not rule_name:\n                continue  # AlertRule mal-configurada\n            \n            # check cooldown via Incident table (incident.alert_rule_id == ar.id, last_triggered)\n            if _on_cooldown(db, ar):\n                continue\n            \n            count = _count_blocks(db, rule_name, web_acl_id, ar.duration)\n            if _operator_check(count, ar.operator, float(ar.threshold)):\n                trigger_alert(\n                    TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK,\n                    title=f\"WAF: {rule_name} blocks elevadas\",\n                    body=f\"{count} blocks em {ar.duration}s (threshold {ar.threshold})\",\n                    severity=ar.severity,\n                    alert_rule_id=ar.id,\n                    metadata={\"rule_name\": rule_name, \"web_acl_id\": web_acl_id, \"count\": count},\n                )\n                triggered_pairs.add((rule_name, web_acl_id))\n        \n        # 2. Fallback 3σ pra pares não cobertos\n        all_pairs = _list_active_pairs(db)  # (rule_name, web_acl_id) com eventos recentes\n        for pair in all_pairs:\n            if pair in triggered_pairs:\n                continue\n            # lógica 3σ original aqui (refatorada)\n            ...\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n```\n\nHelper functions (`_on_cooldown`, `_operator_check`, `_count_blocks`, `_list_active_pairs`) ficam no mesmo arquivo ou em `backend/workers/tasks/waf_helpers.py` (criar se não existir).\n\n### Métricas / observabilidade\n\nAdicionar log INFO em cada disparo:\n```\n[detect_attack_spike] custom_rule_match alert_rule_id=42 rule_name=RateLimit-300-Block web_acl_id=05522... count=145 threshold=100\n[detect_attack_spike] fallback_3sigma rule_name=BadBot-UA web_acl_id=05522... count=892 baseline_mean=12 threshold=89\n```\n\n## Restrições\n\n- Pode assumir Fatia 1 (campos `dimensions` e `web_acl_id`/`web_acl_name` existem)\n- Pode assumir Fatia 4 (método `count_blocks_by_rule` existe — mas se quiser independência, pode fazer query inline e marcar TODO refactor)\n- NÃO mexer em models, endpoints, frontend\n- NÃO criar PR\n- Commits pequenos em português\n\n## Output (<400 palavras)\n\n1. arn:aws:wafv2:us-east-1:123456789012:global/webacl/ACL-WPAdminPRD/abc-uuid\n    Retorna o penúltimo segmento (ACL-WPAdminPRD) — esse é o nome amigável.\n\n    Se o input for None, vazio, ou não )\n            query_id = response[\"queryId\"]\n            logger.info(\n                f\"Started CloudWatch query {query_id} \"\n                f\"label={label} log_group={log_group} region={region}\"\n            )\n            return self._poll_query(logs_client, query_id, label=label, log_group=log_group)\n        except logs_client.exceptions.ResourceNotFoundException:\n            logger.warning(\n                f\"Log group not found — skipping label={label} log_group={log_group} region={region}\"\n            )\n            return []\n        except Exception as e:\n            logger.error(\n                f\"Failed to query label={label} log_group={log_group} region={region}: {e}\"\n            )\n            return []\n\n    def _poll_query(self, client, query_id: str, label: str = \"\", log_group: str = \"\") -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"Poll query until Complete, Failed, or timeout.\"\"\"\n        for _ in range(POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):\n            result = client.get_query_results(queryId=query_id)\n            status = result[\"status\"]\n            if status == \"Complete\":\n                logger.info(\n                    f\"Query {query_id} complete: {len(result['results'])} rows \"\n                    f\"label={label} log_group={log_group}\"\n                )\n                return result[\"results\"]\n            if status in (\"Failed\", \"Cancelled\"):\n                logger.error(\n                    f\"Query {query_id} ended with status={status} \"\n                    f\"label={label} log_group={log_group}\"\n                )\n                return []\n            time.sleep(1)\n        logger.warning(\n            f\"Query {query_id} timed out after {POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s \"\n            f\"label={label} log_group={log_group}\"\n        )\n        return []\n"
}

collect_waf_events  — runs every 5 min, watermark cursor per source
detect_attack_spike — runs every 15 min, Z-score spike detection
"""
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from sqlalchemy import func, select, text
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert as pg_insert

from app.core.sync_database import sync_db_session
from app.models.cloud_account import CloudAccount
from app.models.security_event import SecurityEvent
from app.services.ip_enrichment import IpEnrichmentService
from app.services.waf_collector import WafCollectorService
from workers.celery_app import celery_app

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _get_cloud_account(db) -> CloudAccount:
    """Fetch the active AWS CloudAccount (first active one for now)."""
    from app.core.config import settings

    account_id = getattr(settings, "CONCERTACAO_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID", None)
    if account_id:
        account = db.execute(
            select(CloudAccount).where(CloudAccount.id == int(account_id))
        ).scalar_one_or_none()
        if account:
            return account

    # Fallback: first active AWS account
    from app.models.cloud_account import CloudProvider
    account = db.execute(
        select(CloudAccount).where(
            CloudAccount.provider == CloudProvider.AWS,
            CloudAccount.is_active == True,
        ).limit(1)
    ).scalar_one_or_none()

    if not account:
        raise RuntimeError("No active AWS CloudAccount found in database")
    return account

| # | Origem | Fix |
|---|--------|-----|
| **B1** | A1+A3+A5 | **Drift snake_case** — CLI grava `WebACL/Rule`, frontend/worker leem `rule_name/web_acl_id`. Sem isso, feature inteira não funciona. |
| **B2** | A3 | `GET /alert-rules` filtra hardcoded `(host,docker,rds,alb,cloudfront)` — exclui WAF. |
| **B3** | A1 | `on_conflict_do_nothing` index_elements desatualizado — coleta para após migration. |
| **B4** | A1 | `ADD CONSTRAINT UNIQUE` falha em hypertable comprimida — precisa decompress_chunk. |
| **B5** | A2 | Race condition em upsert — falta `UniqueConstraint("name")` no DB. |
| **B6** | A2 | Mass assignment sem allow-list — defesa em profundidade. |
| **B7** | A4 | TS `AlertRule` interface sem `dimensions` — quebra Fatia 4 silenciosamente. |
| **B8** | A5 | `WAF_SOURCES_JSON` default hardcoded Concertação — outros deploys quebram. |
| **B9** | A5 | `query_waf` engole erro silencioso por horas. |

### 🟡 IMPORTANTES (fix recomendado — 8)
- A1: `dimensions` sem `server_default '{}'`
- A1+A3: CAGG `attack_timeline_1h` validar pós-ALTER
- A2: `dimensions` sem limite tamanho (payload bomb)
- A3: Cooldown JSON path sem índice (Incident.details)
- A3: covered_pairs cobre par mesmo sem fire — silencia anomalias subthreshold
- A3: Fallback 3σ sem rate-limit por par
- A4: AlertRuleUpsert duplica AlertRuleCreate (drift de validação)
- A5: Endpoint upsert sem logger.info create/update

### 🟢 OK (não tocar)
- SQL injection (parameterizado)
- Audit log com diff before/after
- compare_digest correto
- Watermark per-label OK
- Worker no-op com waf_sources=[]
- Migration downgrade OK

'use client'

import { useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import api, {
  AlertRule,
  AlertRuleCreate,
  AlertRuleUpdate,
  AlertRuleListResponse,
} from '@/lib/api'

export function useAlertRules(filters?: {
  resource_type?: string
  is_active?: boolean
}) {
  return useQuery<AlertRuleListResponse>({
    queryKey: ['alert-rules', filters],
    queryFn: async () => {
      const params = new URLSearchParams()
      if (filters?.resource_type) params.append('resource_type', filters.resource_type)
      if (filters?.is_active !== undefined) params.append('is_active', String(filters.is_active))
      const { data } = await api.get(`/api/v1/alert-rules?${params.toString()}`)
      return data
    },
  })
}

export function useCreateAlertRule() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: async (data: AlertRuleCreate) => {
      const { data: response } = await api.post('/api/v1/alert-rules', data)
      return response as AlertRule
    },
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['alert-rules'] })
    },
  })
}

export function useUpdateAlertRule() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: async ({ id, data }: { id: number; data: AlertRuleUpdate }) => {
      const { data: response } = await api.put(`/api/v1/alert-rules/${id}`, data)
      return response as AlertRule
    },
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['alert-rules'] })
    },
  })
}

export function useDeleteAlertRule() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: async (id: number) => {
      await api.delete(`/api/v1/alert-rules/${id}`)
    },
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['alert-rules'] })
    },
  })
}

export function useToggleAlertRule() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: async (id: number) => {
      const { data } = await api.post(`/api/v1/alert-rules/${id}/toggle`)
      return data as AlertRule
    },
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['alert-rules'] })
    },
  })
}

57	        self.client_factory = AWSClientFactory(cloud_account)

59	    def query_waf(self, source: dict, since_timestamp: datetime) -> list[dict]:
60	        """Query a single WAF log source described by `source` config dict.
61	
62	        Args:
63	            source: dict with keys {label, log_group, region, scope, web_acl_id?, web_acl_name?}
64	            since_timestamp: lower bound for events (watermark cursor)
65	
66	        Returns:
67	            List of CloudWatch Logs Insights result rows (each row is a list of
68	            {field, value} dicts). Returns [] on missing log group, query
69	            failure, or timeout — never raises.
70	        """
71	        log_group = source["log_group"]
72	        region = source["region"]
73	        label = source.get("label", log_group)
74	
75	        logs_client = self.client_factory.get_client("logs", region=region)
76	        try:
77	            response = logs_client.start_query(
78	                logGroupName=log_group,
79	                startTime=int(since_timestamp.timestamp()),
80	                endTime=int(datetime.utcnow().timestamp()),
81	                queryString=WAF_QUERY,
82	            )
83	            query_id = response["queryId"]
84	            logger.info(
85	                f"Started CloudWatch query {query_id} "
86	                f"label={label} log_group={log_group} region={region}"
87	            )
88	            return self._poll_query(logs_client, query_id, label=label, log_group=log_group)
89	        except logs_client.exceptions.ResourceNotFoundException:
90	            logger.warning(
91	                f"Log group not found — skipping label={label} log_group={log_group} region={region}"
92	            )
93	            return []
94	        except Exception as e:
95	            logger.error(
96	                f"Failed to query label={label} log_group={log_group} region={region}: {e}"
97	            )
98	            return []
99	
100	    def _poll_query(self, client, query_id: str, label: str = "", log_group: str = "") -> list[dict]:
101	        """Poll query until Complete, Failed, or timeout."""
102	        for _ in range(POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):
103	            result = client.get_query_results(queryId=query_id)
104	            status = result["status"]
105	            if status == "Complete":
106	                logger.info(
107	                    f"Query {query_id} complete: {len(result['results'])} rows "
108	                    f"label={label} log_group={log_group}"
109	                )
110	                return result["results"]
111	            if status in ("Failed", "Cancelled"):
112	                logger.error(
113	                    f"Query {query_id} ended with status={status} "
114	                    f"label={label} log_group={log_group}"

Ciclo 2 completo (5/5). Consolido achados.

## Consolidação Ciclo 2

### 🔴 Bloqueadores novos (3)

**B3-#1 (edge case)** — `WAF_SOURCES_JSON` com `null` no array crasha loop inteiro (AttributeError). Fix: skip não-dict.

**B3-#3 (edge case)** — `AlertRuleUpsert` aceita `dimensions: None` mas model é NOT NULL → IntegrityError loop infinito. Fix: validator coerce `None` → `{}`.

**B4-Elo3 (e2e crítico)** — `_parse_events` ignora `webaclId` extraído do log e usa só config. Em multi-ACL/single-log-group, todos events ficam com `web_acl_id` errado/NULL → Elo 4 quebra → alerts nunca disparam. Fix: priorizar `fields.get("webaclId")` do log com fallback para config.

### 🟡 Importantes (consenso múltiplos auditores)

- B2: 2 tests rápidos antes do PR (allow-list B6, dimensions validator)
- B3-#8: IntegrityError handler genérico mascara bugs não-UNIQUE; inspecionar `constraint_name`
- B3-#6: dois timers de refetch no frontend (setInterval + react-query)
- B4-Elo6: linkagem `findLinkedAlertRule` "frouxa" quando ambos `web_acl_id` null
- B5-#1 **(DX crítico)**: `bit-waf/apply-rule.sh` não chama `upsert_waf_alert.py` — feature inteira fica órfã sem hook

### 🟢 Validados ciclo 2
- B1: 9/9 fixes do ciclo 1 confirmados, zero regressões
- B2: cobertura aceitável com follow-up issue
- Demais elos do flow e2e (1, 2, 5)

## Fixes do ciclo 2

This task writes the values; if the model column\n    doesn't exist yet, SQLAlchemy will raise on insert — coordinated via merge.\n    \"\"\"\n    label = source_config[\"label\"]\n    web_acl_id = source_config.get(\"web_acl_id\")\n    web_acl_name = source_config.get(\"web_acl_name\")\n\n    parsed = []\n    for event in raw_events:\n        fields = {f[\"field\"]: f[\"value\"] for f in event}\n        ts_raw = fields.get(\"@timestamp\", \"\")\n        if not ts_raw:\n            continue\n        try:\n            ts = datetime.fromisoformat(ts_raw.replace(\"Z\", \"+00:00\"))\n        except ValueError:\n            continue\n        parsed.append({\n            \"timestamp\": ts,\n            \"source\": label,\n            \"rule_name\": fields.get(\"terminatingRuleId\"),\n            \"action\": fields.get(\"action\", \"BLOCK\"),\n            \"ip_address\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.clientIp\"),\n            \"user_agent\": fields.get(\"user_agent\"),\n            \"uri\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.uri\"),\n            \"country_code\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.country\"),\n            \"http_method\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.httpMethod\"),\n            \"ip_org\": None,\n            \"ip_city\": None,\n            \"ip_asn\": None,\n            \"web_acl_id\": web_acl_id,\n            \"web_acl_name\": web_acl_name,\n        })\n    return parsed",
  "new_string": "def _parse_events(raw_events: list, source_config: dict) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Convert CloudWatch Logs Insights result rows to dicts for upsert.\n\n    CloudWatch Insights format: [{'field': '@timestamp', 'value': '...'}, ...]\n\n    Resolução de `web_acl_id` / `web_acl_name`:\n      1. **Preferimos** o `webaclId` extraído do log do WAF (campo `webaclId`)\n         — autoritativo, suporta múltiplas ACLs no mesmo log_group.\n      2. Fallback para `web_acl_id` / `web_acl_name` da config do source\n         (útil quando log group cobre 1 ACL ou pra deploys antigos sem\n         `webaclId` no schema do log).\n      `web_acl_name` é derivado do ARN via parse; só usa fallback config\n      se parser não conseguir extrair.\n    \"\"\"\n    label = source_config[\"label\"]\n    config_web_acl_id = source_config.get(\"web_acl_id\")\n    config_web_acl_name = source_config.get(\"web_acl_name\")\n\n    parsed = []\n    for event in raw_events:\n        fields = {f[\"field\"]: f[\"value\"] for f in event}\n        ts_raw = fields.get(\"@timestamp\", \"\")\n        if not ts_raw:\n            continue\n        try:\n            ts = datetime.fromisoformat(ts_raw.replace(\"Z\", \"+00:00\"))\n        except ValueError:\n            continue\n\n        # webaclId do log é autoritativo; config é fallback.\n        log_web_acl_id = fields.get(\"webaclId\")\n        web_acl_id = log_web_acl_id or config_web_acl_id\n        # web_acl_name: parse do ARN, com fallback para config.\n        web_acl_name = parse_web_acl_name_from_arn(log_web_acl_id) or config_web_acl_name\n\n        parsed.append({\n            \"timestamp\": ts,\n            \"source\": label,\n            \"rule_name\": fields.get(\"terminatingRuleId\"),\n            \"action\": fields.get(\"action\", \"BLOCK\"),\n            \"ip_address\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.clientIp\"),\n            \"user_agent\": fields.get(\"user_agent\"),\n            \"uri\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.uri\"),\n            \"country_code\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.country\"),\n            \"http_method\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.httpMethod\"),\n            \"ip_org\": None,\n            \"ip_city\": None,\n            \"ip_asn\": None,\n            \"web_acl_id\": web_acl_id,\n            \"web_acl_name\": web_acl_name,\n        })\n    return parsed"

Antes era frouxo — qualquer null curto-\n    // circuitava match e dava falsa sensação de cobertura quando backend não\n    // dispara alerta de fato.\n    if (!alertRules?.items) return undefined\n    return alertRules.items.find((r) => {\n      const dims = r.dimensions\n      if (!dims) return false\n      if (dims.rule_name !== stat.rule_name) return false\n      // Comparação estrita: ambos preenchidos igual OU ambos ausentes.\n      const dimAcl = dims.web_acl_id ?? null\n      const statAcl = stat.web_acl_id ?? null\n      if (dimAcl !== statAcl) return false\n      return true\n    })\n  }"

**Causa identificada — não é regressão de fix anterior, é vetor novo: YandexBot.**

- **1271 / 1273 (99,8%)** dos 5xx vieram de `YandexBot/3.0`
- Origem: 5 IPs `64.252.x.x` (range CloudFront/AWS — Yandex passa via CF, IPs reais ficam mascarados)
- Padrão: 504 (gateway timeout) — backend PHP travou tentando processar archive pages CCT (`/veiculo/*`, `/2025/*`) — exatamente o vetor JetEngine + WPML que consumiu FPM no incidente Meta-AI 02/05

Mesmo padrão do `meta-externalagent` (incidente 01/05) e do espiral 502 (02/05): bot legítimo ignora cache, dispara floods de archive/listing pages, satura FPM.

**Mitigação — temos rule pronta:**

`bit-nginx-bot-block` (mu-plugin do site no `bit-security-hardening.php` ou nginx map) já bloqueia `meta-externalagent`. Mesmo padrão se aplica a `YandexBot` em archive pages dinâmicas.

Mantemos como estava — Mombak também é Aurora e tem o mesmo padrão de swap. Se quiser que Mombak ganhe os mesmos thresholds custom (512MB / 1GB) em vez de ficar desabilitado, é só pedir e

replico.



Lag de ~6 min do CF 5XX rate



Está dentro do esperado, soma de três cadências independentes:



1. CloudWatch publish lag — CW publica métricas com 1–2 min de atraso da janela

2. Polling cycle do bit-monitoring — Celery beat fetch das métricas CW a cada 5 min

3. Evaluator cycle — evaluate_infra_alerts roda a cada 2 min



Pior caso: ~1-2 + 5 + 2 = 8-9 min. Melhor caso (alinhamento favorável): 3-4 min. Os 6 min observados estão exatamente no meio — sem patologia.



Se quiser apertar isso, há dois ajustes possíveis (mas com trade-offs):



- Reduzir período do CW poller para 1 min: aumenta custo do GetMetricData (CW cobra por API call) e pode esbarrar em rate limit. Faz sentido se o cliente topar o custo extra.

- Reduzir intervalo do evaluator para 1 min: economiza ~1 min no pior caso, custo zero. Possível mexer em produção mas precisa avaliar carga no DB (TimescaleDB lookback queries) —

historicamente 2 min foi o equilíbrio que escolhemos.



Para o caso do espiral 502, o lag de 6 min não é o gargalo (incidente durou 11 min) — o gargalo era o threshold do CF rate diluindo o spike. Com o Target 5XX > 10 ativo agora, o sinal vai

chegar mais rápido também porque thresholds menores cruzam a média mais cedo.

    feat: módulo Attack Monitoring — security_events (WAF CloudFront + ALB)
    
    Implementa monitoramento consolidado de ataques WAF para concertacaoamazonia.com.br.
    
    ## Backend
    - SecurityEvent model (TimescaleDB hypertable, BigInteger PK, UniqueConstraint para deduplicação)
    - WafCollectorService: CloudWatch Logs Insights async (start_query + polling)
    - IpEnrichmentService: ip-api.com + Redis cache 7 dias, rate-limited batches
    - SecurityService: queries agregadas com continuous aggregate attack_timeline_1h
    - 4 endpoints FastAPI: /security/summary, /events, /timeline, /top-attackers
    - Celery task collect_waf_events (5min, watermark cursor +1s)
    - Celery task detect_attack_spike (15min, Z-score amostral 3σ)
    - Alembic migration: hypertable + compressão 7d + retenção 90d + aggregate
    - TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK + CONCERTACAO_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID em config
    
    ## Frontend
    - useSecurityEvents hooks (TanStack Query, 30s/60s refetch)
    - Dashboard /security: KPI cards, timeline BarChart, rules PieChart, top attackers, events table
    - Recharts com dynamic import (ssr: false) para evitar ReferenceError no SSR
    - useWebSocket: listener security_event via useCallback memoizado
    - Paginação robusta com reset ao trocar período
    
    ## Pré-requisitos para ativar
    1. Habilitar logging WAF ALB (aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb) — ver plano Passo 0
    2. alembic upgrade head
    3. Definir CONCERTACAO_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID no .env
    4. Reiniciar workers Celery

> AGENT

Excelente — master já tem **discovery de WAF Web ACLs** como `Resource`. import enum
from sqlalchemy import (
    Column,
    Integer,
    String,
    Boolean,
    Text,
    DateTime,
    ForeignKey,
    Enum,
    JSON,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
from sqlalchemy.sql import func

from app.core.database import Base


class TriggerType(str, enum.Enum):
    """Types of events that can trigger notifications."""
    MONITOR_DOWN = "monitor_down"
    MONITOR_UP = "monitor_up"
    MONITOR_DEGRADED = "monitor_degraded"
    SSL_EXPIRING = "ssl_expiring"
    SSL_EXPIRED = "ssl_expired"
    RESOURCE_UNHEALTHY = "resource_unhealthy"
    RESOURCE_CREATED = "resource_created"
    RESOURCE_DELETED = "resource_deleted"
    DISCOVERY_COMPLETE = "discovery_complete"
    DISCOVERY_FAILED = "discovery_failed"
    BUDGET_THRESHOLD = "budget_threshold"
    BUDGET_EXCEEDED = "budget_exceeded"
    HOST_METRIC_THRESHOLD = "host_metric_threshold"
    CONTAINER_METRIC_THRESHOLD = "container_metric_threshold"
    CLOUDWATCH_METRIC_THRESHOLD = "cloudwatch_metric_threshold"

    SECURITY_ATTACK = "security_attack"
>>>>>>> 6e3e687 (feat: módulo Attack Monitoring — security_events (WAF CloudFront + ALB))


class Severity(str, enum.Enum):
    """Alert severity levels."""
    CRITICAL = "critical"
    WARNING = "warning"
    INFO = "info"


class NotificationRule(Base):
    """
    Notification rules define when and how to send alerts.

    Each rule specifies:
    - What event triggers the notification (trigger_type)
    - What severity levels to match (severity_filter)
    - Which channels to notify (channel_ids)
    - Optional conditions (e.g., specific monitors, resources)
    """
    __tablename__ = "notification_rules"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    name = Column(String(255), nullable=False)
    description = Column(Text, nullable=True)

    # Trigger configuration
    trigger_type = Column(Enum(TriggerType), nullable=False)
    severity_filter = Column(JSON, nullable=True)  # List of severities to match, null = all

    # Conditions (optional filters)
    conditions = Column(JSON, nullable=True)
    # Example conditions:
    # {
    #   "monitor_ids": [1, 2, 3],  # Only for specific monitors
    #   "resource_types": ["ec2", "rds"],  # Only for specific resource types
    #   "cloud_account_ids": [1],  # Only for specific accounts
    #   "ssl_days_threshold": 14,  # SSL expiring within X days
    # }

    # Channels to notify (list of channel IDs)
    channel_ids = Column(JSON, nullable=False)  # List of notification_channel IDs

    # Notification settings
    cooldown_minutes = Column(Integer, default=0)  # Min time between repeated alerts (0 = disabled, rely on threshold)
    include_details = Column(Boolean, default=True)  # Include full details in notification

    # Custom message templates (optional - uses defaults if not set)
    # Supports variables like {{monitor_name}}, {{status}}, {{url}}, {{error}}, etc.
    message_subject = Column(String(500), nullable=True)  # Email subject / notification title
    message_body = Column(Text, nullable=True)  # Full message body (supports HTML for email)

    # Status
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True, nullable=False, index=True)
    last_triggered = Column(DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)
    trigger_count = Column(Integer, default=0)

    # Timestamps
    created_at = Column(DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now())
    updated_at = Column(DateTime(timezone=True), onupdate=func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<NotificationRule(id={self.id}, name='{self.name}', trigger='{self.trigger_type}')>"

11	- attack_timeline_1h continuous aggregate (5-min refresh)
12	- security_attack value in triggertype PostgreSQL enum

"""Celery tasks for WAF log collection and attack spike detection.

collect_waf_events  — runs every 5 min, watermark cursor per source
detect_attack_spike — runs every 15 min, Z-score spike detection
"""
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from sqlalchemy import func, select, text
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert as pg_insert

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _get_cloud_account(db) -> CloudAccount:
    """Fetch the active AWS CloudAccount (first active one for now)."""
    from app.core.config import settings

    account_id = getattr(settings, "CONCERTACAO_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID", None)
    if account_id:
        account = db.execute(
            select(CloudAccount).where(CloudAccount.id == int(account_id))
        ).scalar_one_or_none()
        if account:
            return account

    # Fallback: first active AWS account
    from app.models.cloud_account import CloudProvider
    account = db.execute(
        select(CloudAccount).where(
            CloudAccount.provider == CloudProvider.AWS,
            CloudAccount.is_active == True,
        ).limit(1)
    ).scalar_one_or_none()

    if not account:
        raise RuntimeError("No active AWS CloudAccount found in database")
    return account


def _parse_events(raw_events: list, source: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Convert CloudWatch Logs Insights result rows to dicts for upsert.

    CloudWatch Insights format: [{'field': '@timestamp', 'value': '...'}, ...]
    """
    parsed = []
    for event in raw_events:
        fields = {f["field"]: f["value"] for f in event}
        ts_raw = fields.get("@timestamp", "")
        if not ts_raw:
            continue
        try:
            ts = datetime.fromisoformat(ts_raw.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        except ValueError:
            continue
        parsed.append({
            "timestamp": ts,
            "source": source,
            "rule_name": fields.get("terminatingRuleId"),

            "ip_address": fields.get("httpRequest.clientIp"),

            "uri": fields.get("httpRequest.uri"),
            "country_code": fields.get("httpRequest.country"),
            "http_method": fields.get("httpRequest.httpMethod"),
            "ip_org": None,
            "ip_city": None,
            "ip_asn": None,

**Plano de generalização** — vou adotar abordagem simples e idiomática que o engenheiro pediu:

1. Adicionar coluna `waf_monitoring_enabled` em `CloudAccount` (default `False`, opt-in explícito)
2. Cada `CloudAccount` opt-in tem campo `waf_log_groups` (JSON: `[{"label", "log_group", "region", "scope", "web_acl_arn"}, ...]`) — config-driven ao invés de log groups hardcoded
3. Refatorar `collect_waf_events` para iterar sobre **todas** CloudAccounts com `waf_monitoring_enabled=True`
4. Refatorar `WafCollectorService` para receber `log_groups` por instância (não constantes globais)
5. Remover `CONCERTACAO_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID` do config

Mas faço isso **em commit separado** (não dentro do cherry-pick). Primeiro completo o cherry-pick limpo, depois aplico generalização como segundo commit, depois rebase os outros 3 fixes do PR #180 (que viraram supérfluos pois o waf vai ficar generalizado).

1	"""WAF log collector — queries CloudWatch Logs Insights for WAF BLOCK events.
2	
3	Supports both CloudFront WAF (aws-waf-logs-concertacao) and
4	ALB WAF (aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb) log groups.
5	
6	CloudWatch Logs Insights is ASYNC: start_query + poll for completion.
7	Watermark cursor: queries only NEW events since last processed timestamp.
8	"""
9	import logging
10	import time
11	from datetime import datetime
12	
13	from app.models.cloud_account import CloudAccount
14	from app.providers.aws.client import AWSClientFactory
15	
16	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
17	
18	CLOUDFRONT_LOG_GROUP = "aws-waf-logs-concertacao"
19	ALB_LOG_GROUP = "aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb"
20	POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60
21	
22	WAF_QUERY = """
23	fields @timestamp, action, terminatingRuleId,
24	       httpRequest.clientIp, httpRequest.uri, httpRequest.country,
25	       httpRequest.httpMethod,
26	       httpRequest.headers.0.value as user_agent
27	| filter action = 'BLOCK'
28	| sort @timestamp asc
29	| limit 10000
30	"""
31	
32	
33	class WafCollectorService:
34	    def __init__(self, cloud_account: CloudAccount):
35	        self.client_factory = AWSClientFactory(cloud_account)
36	        self.region = "sa-east-1"
37	
38	    def query_cloudfront_waf(self, since_timestamp: datetime) -> list[dict]:
39	        return self._query_waf_logs(CLOUDFRONT_LOG_GROUP, since_timestamp)
40	
41	    def query_alb_waf(self, since_timestamp: datetime) -> list[dict]:
42	        return self._query_waf_logs(ALB_LOG_GROUP, since_timestamp)
43	
44	    def _query_waf_logs(self, log_group: str, since_timestamp: datetime) -> list[dict]:
45	        """Start a CloudWatch Logs Insights query and poll until complete."""
46	        logs_client = self.client_factory.get_client("logs", region=self.region)
47	        try:
48	            response = logs_client.start_query(
49	                logGroupName=log_group,
50	                startTime=int(since_timestamp.timestamp()),
51	                endTime=int(datetime.utcnow().timestamp()),
52	                queryString=WAF_QUERY,
53	            )
54	            query_id = response["queryId"]
55	            logger.info(f"Started CloudWatch query {query_id} on {log_group}")
56	            return self._poll_query(logs_client, query_id)
57	        except logs_client.exceptions.ResourceNotFoundException:
58	            logger.warning(f"Log group {log_group} not found — skipping")
59	            return []
60	        except Exception as e:
61	            logger.error(f"Failed to query {log_group}: {e}")
62	            return []
63	
64	    def _poll_query(self, client, query_id: str) -> list[dict]:
65	        """Poll query until Complete, Failed, or timeout."""
66	        for _ in range(POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):
67	            result = client.get_query_results(queryId=query_id)
68	            status = result["status"]
69	            if status == "Complete":
70	                logger.info(f"Query {query_id} complete: {len(result['results'])} rows")
71	                return result["results"]
72	            if status in ("Failed", "Cancelled"):
73	                logger.error(f"Query {query_id} ended with status: {status}")
74	                return []
75	            time.sleep(1)
76	        logger.warning(f"Query {query_id} timed out after {POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s")
77	        return []
78

{
  "file_path": "/Users/dcambria/scripts/bit-monitoring/backend/app/services/waf_collector.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"WAF log collector — queries CloudWatch Logs Insights for WAF BLOCK events.\n\nConfig-driven por CloudAccount: cada conta opt-in (waf_monitoring_enabled=True)\ndeclara seus log groups em waf_log_groups (JSON). Cada entry é uma fonte:\n  {\n    \"label\": \"waf_cloudfront_concertacao\",  # globally unique key (SecurityEvent.source)\n    \"log_group\": \"aws-waf-logs-concertacao\",\n    \"region\": \"us-east-1\",                  # CF WAF logs sempre us-east-1\n    \"scope\": \"CLOUDFRONT\",                  # ou \"REGIONAL\"\n    \"web_acl_arn\": \"arn:aws:wafv2:...\"      # opcional, deriva web_acl_id/name\n  }\n\nCloudWatch Logs Insights é ASYNC: start_query + poll until complete.\nWatermark cursor (per-source label): queries only NEW events since last processed.\n\"\"\"\nimport logging\nimport time\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom app.models.cloud_account import CloudAccount\nfrom app.providers.aws.client import AWSClientFactory\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nPOLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60\n\n# webaclId no fields permite distinguir mesma rule em ACLs diferentes.\nWAF_QUERY = \"\"\"\nfields @timestamp, action, terminatingRuleId, webaclId,\n       httpRequest.clientIp, httpRequest.uri, httpRequest.country,\n       httpRequest.httpMethod,\n       httpRequest.headers.0.value as user_agent\n| filter action = 'BLOCK'\n| sort @timestamp asc\n| limit 10000\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef parse_web_acl_name_from_arn(web_acl_arn: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:\n    \"\"\"Extrai nome legível do Web ACL a partir do ARN.\n\n    Formato: arn:aws:wafv2:us-east-1:123:global/webacl/ACL-Name/uuid\n    Retorna o penúltimo segmento (nome amigável) ou None se malformado.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not web_acl_arn:\n        return None\n    parts = web_acl_arn.split(\"/\")\n    if len(parts) >= 2:\n        candidate = parts[-2]\n        if candidate and candidate not in (\"webacl\", \"regional\"):\n            return candidate\n    return None\n\n\nclass WafCollectorService:\n    \"\"\"Per-CloudAccount WAF log collector.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, cloud_account: CloudAccount):\n        self.cloud_account = cloud_account\n        self.client_factory = AWSClientFactory(cloud_account)\n\n    def query_waf(self, source_config: dict, since_timestamp: datetime) -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"Query a single WAF log source.\n\n        Args:\n            source_config: {label, log_group, region, scope, web_acl_arn?}\n            since_timestamp: lower bound for events (watermark cursor)\n\n        Returns:\n            List of CloudWatch Logs Insights result rows. Empty list on\n            ResourceNotFoundException, query failure, or timeout — never raises\n            (silent degradation in collector path).\n        \"\"\"\n        log_group = source_config[\"log_group\"]\n        region = source_config[\"region\"]\n        label = source_config.get(\"label\", log_group)\n\n        t0 = time.monotonic()\n        logs_client = self.client_factory.get_client(\"logs\", region=region)\n        try:\n            response = logs_client.start_query(\n                logGroupName=log_group,\n                startTime=int(since_timestamp.timestamp()),\n                endTime=int(datetime.utcnow().timestamp()),\n                queryString=WAF_QUERY,\n            )\n            query_id = response[\"queryId\"]\n            logger.info(\n                f\"Started CloudWatch query {query_id} \"\n                f\"label={label} log_group={log_group} region={region} \"\n                f\"account={self.cloud_account.id}\"\n            )\n            return self._poll_query(\n                logs_client, query_id, label=label, log_group=log_group, t0=t0\n            )\n        except logs_client.exceptions.ResourceNotFoundException:\n            logger.warning(\n                f\"Log group not found — skipping label={label} \"\n                f\"log_group={log_group} region={region}\"\n            )\n            return []\n        except Exception as e:\n            # CRITICAL: degradação silenciosa = dashboards mostrarão zero blocks,\n            # cenário pior do que \"DOWN\". Eleva pra meta-monitoring.\n            logger.critical(\n                f\"WAF query failed (silent collector degradation risk) \"\n                f\"label={label} log_group={log_group} region={region} \"\n                f\"elapsed_ms={int((time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000)} error={e}\"\n            )\n            return []\n\n    def _poll_query(\n        self,\n        client,\n        query_id: str,\n        label: str = \"\",\n        log_group: str = \"\",\n        t0: Optional[float] = None,\n    ) -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"Poll query until Complete, Failed, or timeout.\"\"\"\n        for _ in range(POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):\n            result = client.get_query_results(queryId=query_id)\n            status = result[\"status\"]\n            if status == \"Complete\":\n                elapsed_ms = int((time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000) if t0 else -1\n                stats = result.get(\"statistics\", {})\n                logger.info(\n                    f\"Query {query_id} complete rows={len(result['results'])} \"\n                    f\"elapsed_ms={elapsed_ms} \"\n                    f\"bytes_scanned={stats.get('bytesScanned', 'n/a')} \"\n                    f\"records_matched={stats.get('recordsMatched', 'n/a')} \"\n                    f\"label={label} log_group={log_group}\"\n                )\n                return result[\"results\"]\n            if status in (\"Failed\", \"Cancelled\"):\n                logger.critical(\n                    f\"WAF query {query_id} ended with status={status} \"\n                    f\"(silent collector degradation) \"\n                    f\"label={label} log_group={log_group}\"\n                )\n                return []\n            time.sleep(1)\n        logger.critical(\n            f\"WAF query {query_id} timed out after {POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s \"\n            f\"(silent collector degradation) \"\n            f\"label={label} log_group={log_group}\"\n        )\n        return []\n"
}

80	@celery_app.task(name="workers.tasks.waf_collector.collect_waf_events")
81	def collect_waf_events():
82	    """Collect WAF BLOCK events from CloudFront and ALB WAF logs.
83	
84	    Uses watermark cursor per source. Watermark advances by +1s after the last
85	    processed event to avoid re-fetching the boundary event. Upserts with
86	    on_conflict_do_nothing (requires uq_se_source_ts_ip_rule constraint).
87	    RealtimeService.publish_event_sync is called OUTSIDE the db session to
88	    avoid double-commit issues with sync_db_session context manager.
89	    """
90	    new_event_count = 0
91	
92	    with sync_db_session() as db:
93	        try:
94	            cloud_account = _get_cloud_account(db)
95	        except RuntimeError as e:
96	            logger.error(f"collect_waf_events: {e}")
97	            return
98	
99	        collector = WafCollectorService(cloud_account)
100	        enricher = IpEnrichmentService()
101	
102	        for source, fetch_fn in [
103	            ("waf_cloudfront", collector.query_cloudfront_waf),
104	            ("waf_alb", collector.query_alb_waf),
105	        ]:
106	            last_ts = db.execute(
107	                select(func.max(SecurityEvent.timestamp)).where(
108	                    SecurityEvent.source == source
109	                )
110	            ).scalar()
111	
112	            if last_ts:
113	                # Advance by 1s to exclude the already-processed boundary event
114	                since = last_ts + timedelta(seconds=1)
115	            else:
116	                since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=6)
117	
118	            logger.info(f"Fetching {source} events since {since.isoformat()}")
119	            raw = fetch_fn(since_timestamp=since)
120	            if not raw:
121	                logger.info(f"No new events for {source}")
122	                continue
123	
124	            parsed = _parse_events(raw, source)
125	            if not parsed:
126	                continue
127	
128	            # Enrich IPs
129	            unique_ips = list({e["ip_address"] for e in parsed if e.get("ip_address")})
130	            enrichments = enricher.enrich_batch(unique_ips)
131	
132	            for event in parsed:
133	                ip = event.get("ip_address")
134	                if ip and ip in enrichments:
135	                    geo = enrichments[ip]
136	                    event["ip_org"] = geo.get("org")
137	                    event["ip_city"] = geo.get("city")
138	                    event["ip_asn"] = geo.get("as")
139	                    if not event.get("country_code"):
140	                        event["country_code"] = geo.get("countryCode")
141	
142	            # on_conflict_do_nothing requires the uq_se_source_ts_ip_rule constraint
143	            stmt = (
144	                pg_insert(SecurityEvent)
145	                .values(parsed)
146	                .on_conflict_do_nothing(
147	                    index_elements=["source", "timestamp", "ip_address", "rule_name"]
148	                )
149	            )
150	            db.execute(stmt)
151	            new_event_count += len(parsed)
152	            logger.info(f"Upserted {len(parsed)} {source} events")
153	
154	        # sync_db_session commits automatically on __exit__ — no manual commit needed
155	
156	    # Publish real-time event OUTSIDE the db session to avoid double-commit
157	    if new_event_count > 0:
158	        from app.services.realtime import RealtimeService
159	        RealtimeService.publish_event_sync(
160	            event_type="security_event",
161	            data={"timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()},
162	            target_user_ids=None,
163	        )

app.models.security_event import SecurityEvent\nfrom app.services.ip_enrichment import IpEnrichmentService\nfrom app.services.waf_collector import WafCollectorService\nfrom workers.celery_app import celery_app\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef _list_waf_enabled_accounts(db) -> list[CloudAccount]:\n    \"\"\"Lista CloudAccounts AWS opt-in para coleta WAF.\n\n    Mesmo padrão de cloudwatch_enabled e backups_monitoring_enabled — opt-in\n    explícito por conta, evita custo CloudWatch Insights em deploys que não\n    precisam de WAF monitoring.\n    \"\"\"\n    return list(\n        db.execute(\n            select(CloudAccount).where(\n                CloudAccount.provider == CloudProvider.AWS,\n                CloudAccount.is_active == True,\n                CloudAccount.waf_monitoring_enabled == True,\n            )\n        ).scalars()\n    )\n\n\ndef _parse_events(raw_events: list, source_config: dict) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Convert CloudWatch Logs Insights result rows to dicts for upsert.\n\n    CloudWatch Insights format: [{'field': '@timestamp', 'value': '...'}, ...]\n    \"\"\"\n    label = source_config[\"label\"]\n    parsed = []\n    for event in raw_events:\n        fields = {f[\"field\"]: f[\"value\"] for f in event}\n        ts_raw = fields.get(\"@timestamp\", \"\")\n        if not ts_raw:\n            continue\n        try:\n            ts = datetime.fromisoformat(ts_raw.replace(\"Z\", \"+00:00\"))\n        except ValueError:\n            continue\n        parsed.append({\n            \"timestamp\": ts,\n            \"source\": label,\n            \"rule_name\": fields.get(\"terminatingRuleId\"),\n            \"action\": fields.get(\"action\", \"BLOCK\"),\n            \"ip_address\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.clientIp\"),\n            \"user_agent\": fields.get(\"user_agent\"),\n            \"uri\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.uri\"),\n            \"country_code\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.country\"),\n            \"http_method\": fields.get(\"httpRequest.httpMethod\"),\n            \"ip_org\": None,\n            \"ip_city\": None,\n            \"ip_asn\": None,\n        })\n    return parsed"
}

> AGENT

**Bug real**: `resource_id="concertacao"` hardcoded no spike alert. Isso anula a generalização. Em deploy multi-tenant, todos alertas WAF apontam pra "concertacao". Vou corrigir.

Mas há um problema de design: `detect_attack_spike` lê eventos de **todas** as accounts (sem filtrar por source/account) e dispara **um** alerta global. Isso é incoerente com a generalização — em multi-tenant, alertas precisam ser por account. Vejo a função inteira:

> AGENT

Confirmado o que suspeitava. **Essa função tem 2 bugs de generalização:**

1. **Query global** (sem filtro por source/account) — em multi-tenant, agrega eventos de todas accounts num único alerta. Mistura sinais de clientes diferentes.
2. **`resource_id="concertacao"`** hardcoded — todos alertas apontam pra "concertacao" mesmo em outras contas.

A correção certa: iterar por source (label) e disparar alerta por source com `resource_id={label}`. Source é a chave globalmente única declarada em `waf_log_groups`.

Detalhes abaixo.\n\n---\n\n### 🔴 BLOQUEANTE 1 — `SecurityEvent` sem `cloud_account_id` (vazamento de dados entre clientes)\n\n`backend/app/models/security_event.py` — o modelo não tem FK para `cloud_account_id`. Como consequência, todos os endpoints da `SecurityService` (`/api/v1/security/events`, `/summary`, `/timeline`, `/top-attackers`) retornam eventos de **todas** as contas opt-in misturados, sem filtro de conta.\n\nQuando Biomas (ou qualquer outro cliente) fizer opt-in, um admin de Biomas chamando `GET /api/v1/security/events` verá eventos WAF da Concertação, e vice-versa. Não existe nenhum mecanismo de isolamento.\n\n**Correção necessária**:\n1. Adicionar `cloud_account_id INTEGER NOT NULL` (FK para `cloud_accounts.id`) ao modelo + migration\n2.
